Wastewater quality study at student's cafetaria, Universiti Malaysia Pahang /
Project paper (Bachelor of Civil Engineering) -- Universiti Malaysia Pahang - 2007

Nowadays, water pollution problem has become serious national issues. The increasing of solid wastes, oil and grease generated from cafeterias or restaurants also had contributed to this problem. Cafeteria that operated daily in Universiti Malaysia Pahang (UMP) generates lots of food waste, oil and grease and could produced water pollution. A study was conducted to evaluate the quality of wastewater from the cafeteria. Two main objectives of the study are to evaluate the quality of wastewater from UMP student's cafeteria and to determine the effectiveness of sullage trap built at UMP student's cafeteria. Wastewater from three points were taken and tested in UMP's Environmental Laboratory. The parameters tested are pH, Suspended Solids (SS), Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD), Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD), Oil and Grease, Ammonia Nitrogen (AN), Nitrite and Nitrate. Observation is also conducted to evaluate the performance of the trap. The results of test for the sample at inlet and outlet of the trap is compared to determine the effectiveness of trap and the sample of wastewater at point three, which is before it is being released to main drain and then directly to stream is evaluated according to the Environmental Quality Act 1974. The overall results indicate that the performance of the sullage trap is not satisfactory and most of the results of wastewater discharged did not fulfill the requirements stated in the Standard B of Environmental Quality Act 1974. The most critical parameter is oil and grease where the highest value of oil and grease recorded for the effluent is 503.7 mg/L. The second critical parameter is COD which is the highest value recorded was 847 mg/L for point three. It is 88% higher than the allowable value stated in Standard B, Environmental Quality Act 1974 which is 100 mg/L. Several actions must be taken in order to improve the wastewater quality and at the same time to control the sources of pollution. -Author
Removal of heavy metals from petrochemical wastewater by using phytoremediation at Gebeng, Kuantan /
Project paper (Bachelor of Civil Engineering) -- Universiti Malaysia Pahang - 2007

Wastewater pollution has always been a major problem throughout the world. The effects of the wastewater pollution not only occur on human health but also the ecosystem even the extinction of rarely species of aquatic wildlife. The treatments for wastewater pollution are needed to control and manage the severely pollution problems all over the world especially in Malaysia. Phytoremediation is a suitable method because it is clean, efficient, inexpensive (low capital and operating costs), and no environmental disrupted. This technology uses the plants to absorb the pollutants or contaminants is greatly encouraged and promoted by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. In this case, Typha angustifolia will be determined on its potential as suitable plant in phytoremediation. The objectives of this research will focus on evaluation about how effectiveness of phytoremediation to remove the heavy metals which are lead and copper in petrochemical effluent. The study was carried out about 5 month's times which started from April until September 2007. The plants were obtained from Gebeng roadside and started the planting process. The sampling method was carried out 3 times a week. There were other parameters than heavy metals used to measure the effectiveness of phytoremediation in cleaning up the pollutants like BOD, COD, DO, Turbidity, Oil & Grease, pH, Ammonia and Nitrate. Typha angustifolia is a suitable plant to carry out phytoremediation which successfully absorbed over 70% of the lead contaminants in petrochemical effluent from Kaneka (M) Sdn Bhd. Besides that, the content of copper in the petrochemical effluent also was reduced over 80% by using phytoremediation. The result proved that phytoremediation is an effective method to remove the heavy metals especially lead and copper by Typha angustifolia. Typha angustifolia's growth rate was measured and the plant was grown about 0.38m average height after 10 weeks long. -Author
Phytoremediation process in treatment of domestic wastewater using salvania sp., parrot sp. and lysimachia sp. /
Project paper (Bachelor of Civil Engineering) -- Universiti Malaysia Pahang - 2007

In this era of complex and modem technology, water pollution has become a severe problem for the world to cope with. Enormous expenditure has been delivered to resolve this serious matter. Unfortunately, most of the efforts are to no avail without the people's awareness and responsibility towards clean environment. To prevent this phenomenon from continuing spread, researchers have found a solution by using the power of nature. It is called Phytoremediation. This concept is an improvised technique from the wetland system. The system is an alternative in wastewater engineering especially for water treatment. The water treatment act as secondary filter to our wastewater after the treatment process is complete. Uniquely, the wetland system can operate by itself without much maintenance works. This study was conducted to explore the feasibility of using plants species to remediate effluent from domestic wastewater. To achieve the objective, three selected plant species has been chosen for this project. The plants were Salvinia minima (Pokok Kiambang), Parrots Feather ( Pokok Deduit ) and Lysimachia Nummularia Aurea (Pokok Ekor Kucing). All this plant is tested with wastewater from Taman Tasik Bandar and Universiti Malaysia Pahang (UMP) treatment plant effluent for four weeks. The water parameters that has been monitored were BOD, COD, DO, Oil and Grease, Nitrate, pH and Suspended Solids. From the overall experiment results, we found that Parrots Feather specoes contribute the highest removal percentage as follows, for BOD is 5.4%, 11.8% for COD, 4.6% for DO, 8.1 % for Suspended Solids, 15.6% for Oil & Grease and 15.3% for nitrate. Thus, among the three species selected for this research, Parrots Feather species ( Pokok Deduit ) is the most suitable plant in the removal of most water parameters. -Author

There are many procedures that can be implemented in set-up the weather station and one of them is in using the Integrated Sensor Suite (ISS) and transfers the hydrology data using Vantage Pro2 Console and Weatherlink software. This project is involved the process of build the fence and base, the weather station setup, implementation of hardware and software and analysis of data. The data collected by Integrated Sensor Suite will be transfer into the Vantage Pr02 Console. Everything about the hydrology data can be adjusting using the Vantage Pr02 Console. The Weatherlink software can use for shows the graph plotted and the hydrology patterns in graph or chart. Patchouli oil extraction by using hydro distillation (lab scale) /
Patchouli oil extraction by using hydro distillation (lab scale)
Project paper (Bachelor of Chemical Engineering) --- Universiti Malaysia Pahang - 2008

Patchouli or its scientific name Pogostemon cablin, is used in variety of field. For example it is used in Pharmaceutical industry as effective for fungal or bacterial infection and is of great help for insect bite. Patchouli essential oil is mostly used in perfumery industry as product of cosmetic and fragrance oil. The objectives of this research are to study the effect of extraction time and particle size of the leave on the yield of patchouli essential oil. Effects of extraction time and particle size (grinded and non grinded leave) were studied on the yield of patchouli essential oil. The extraction process is performed by using hydro distillation method. Extraction time is varied at 1, 2, 3 and 4 hours and the extraction process is repeated several times on grinded and non grinded patchouli leave. The essential oil obtained, was analyzed by using GC-MS. From the result, the yield of patchouli essential oil is increased as extraction time increased for both grinded and non grinded leave. The highest yield of grinded and non grinded patchouli leave is at four hours in which 1.32% and 0.89% of yield was obtained respectively. From the result also, grinded patchouli leave produces more oil than non grinded patchouli leave. Author

Wastewater come from industry containing mercury is very dangerous. We need to treat the wastewater effectively to avoid the toxic. Membrane usage in wastewater treatment has increase due to its ability to filtrate the unwanted particle. The manipulating of parameters of membrane can give the better result other then changing the type of membrane for filtration of mercury in wastewater. Using P.putida as the pretreatment or volatilizing agent and continue with alternation of pH value for mercury solution, this technique seems easily can reach the target of removing mercury to the minimum level of permitted. datafield.subfield: Effect of build orientation on mechanical properties of epoxy resin reinforced coconut fiber /
Effect of build orientation on mechanical properties of epoxy resin reinforced coconut fiber
Project paper (Bachelor of Mechanical Engineering) -- Universiti Malaysia Pahang - 2009

Composite materials and layered structures based on natural plant fibers are increasingly regarded as an alternative to glass fiber reinforced parts. One of their major fields of application can be found in structural components for the automotive industry. Product examples are door trim panels or instrument panels. For such applications utmost impact strength is required in order to implement a maximum of passenger safety by a good crash behavior. This study is carried out to investigate the mechanical properties of epoxy resin reinforced coconut fiber and describes the effect of build orientation or arrangement parameters based on tensile testing of the process conditions on this important composite characteristic. From the experiment, it was found that the addition of the coconut fiber into polymer matrix had increased the tensile strength of the composite. But, the tensile strains of the composites are decreasing when the fiber is added into the polymer matrix. However, the modulus of elasticity of the reinforced epoxy is increased compared to unreinforced epoxy.
